purpose: Telotristat ethyl is used to treat diarrhea caused by carcinoid syndrome, a condition that happens with certain types of slow-growing tumors called carcinoid tumors. It is used along with somatostatin analog therapy, like octreotide, when that medicine alone is not controlling the diarrhea well enough. It helps reduce the number of bowel movements and improve your quality of life.
how_it_works: Your carcinoid tumor makes too much serotonin, a chemical that speeds up your gut and causes diarrhea. Telotristat ethyl works by blocking an enzyme in the gut called tryptophan hydroxylase, which is needed to make serotonin. By lowering serotonin production in the gut, it helps slow down bowel activity and reduce diarrhea.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, headache, increased liver enzyme levels (seen on blood tests), feeling tired, decreased appetite, gas, swelling in your hands or feet, and constipation. Some patients notice their stools become harder or less frequent.
warnings: Tell your doctor right away if you have severe constipation, as this can sometimes be serious. This medicine may affect liver function, so your doctor will likely check your liver with blood tests while you are on it. Let your doctor know all other medications you take, because telotristat can affect how some other drugs work in your body. It is not recommended during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless your doctor decides the benefit outweighs the risk.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 250 mg taken by mouth three times a day with food. It is important to take it with a meal to help your body absorb it properly. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
